lines: Choose Go to the start line, and the race opens full screen: your bike, a map, and thirty minutes on the clock.
Along the top: the map and its route, whom you race, your bike, and the clock, out of thirty minutes.
Power is the biggest number. Three hundred and seventy-one watts against a target of four eighteen: forty-seven under.
The interval panel: work, one of eight, twenty-nine seconds left, and what comes next. A screen reader hears the time in words.
Each segment's level goes to the bike as it starts: eight for the warm-up, twenty-four for the effort, six to recover.
The route profile comes from the main branch, copied as it is. The road eases towards the world's grade, giving the climb and the metres climbed.
Speed comes from your power, ten times the cube root of watts over twenty. Its sum is the distance you have ridden.
Lower and Raise send the next level as your own, and switch off while the bike is away.
A phone keeps the world, power and the interval. From a laptop, every panel, the bottom row in three columns.
What the tests prove: eighty-two behaviour specs, the route profile and the speed in unit tests, all green, and the first bundle unchanged.
Telo Ride, from the Telo family, turns a smart bike at home into a game.
It pairs with the bike over Bluetooth, reads your power and sets resistance for every hill and interval.

lines.text: Two doors: Race, ride a map against your best-time ghost, bots or people; and Classes, ride along to a video, alone or with a group; fed by one progression of XP, rider levels, stars and map unlocks.
